articles.title: Recital del Kids&Us Manresa ante un flojo Roma Basketball (108-88)
articles.standfirst: Benite (24+5+7), Ongenda (20+7) y Oriola (19+3) y Bassas (13+5 asistencias), destacados
articles.summary: Benite (24+5+7), Ongenda (20+7) y Oriola (19+3) y Bassas (13+5 asistencias), destacados
articles.body: El Kids&Us Manresa se divirtió ante un flojo BC Roma después de derrotar con contundencia a los italianos por 108-88 en un choque dominado de principio a fin por los de Diego Ocampo. La tripleta formada por el base Hugo Benitez y los pívots Pierre Oriola y Nick Ongenda (63 puntos en total entre ellos) fue clave para que su equipo lograra una victoria plácida con un 'basket-average' que puede ser clave en futuros hipotéticos empates en la clasificación de la fase de grupos. Los primeros minutos de partido fueron los únicos donde los romanos tuvieron un acierto notable en ataque gracias a unos buenos minutos del exbaskonista Nico Mannion, que empezó bien desde la línea de tres (12-13, min. 5). Sin embargo, desde ese instante, los manresanos fueron muy superiores, especialmente en el juego interior. El primero en destacar fue Nick Ongenda, que con su habitual juego de pies, puso en problemas a la defensa de los visitantes y abrió la primera gran ventaja del encuentro (23-14, min. 7). Los locales no sólo mantuvieron la ventaja en los minutos posteriores, sino que también fueron capaces de aumentarla y finalmente acabaron con un 32-21 al final del primer cuarto. El guión no cambió en el segundo periodo, y el Kids&Us Manresa continuó con su superioridad bajo aros, pero ahora con otro protagonista, Pierre Oriola, que anotó tanto cerca de la canasta como desde el triple (41-29, min. 13). El BC Roma intentó rebajar la desventaja lo antes posible, pero cuando lo consiguió, de nuevo apareció el propio Oriola para volver al +10 y hacer daño a los italianos, que vieron como la velocidad del rival era superior a la suya (50-40, min. 18). En un cuarto con tanta anotación, los catalanes mantuvieron la ventaja y se fueron al descanso con 57 puntos anotados, frente a los 46 de los romanos, por lo que la afición manresana pudo disfrutar más que en los partidos anteriores. En la reanudación, el Kids&Us Manresa puso la sexta marcha en el acelerador y en un abrir y cerrar de ojos logró una ventaja de 15 puntos tras otro triple, esta vez de Ferran Bassas (70-55, min. 25). Sin embargo, cuando parecía que los catalanes podían romper el partido, el BC Roma encontró el acierto desde el triple gracias a Davis Jr, e incluso lograron ponerse por debajo de los diez puntos de desventaja, situación que provocó el tiempo muerto de Ocampo (74-65, min. 28). Desde entonces, un intercambio de canastas reinó en el Nou Congost, que finalmente benefició a los locales tras los últimos fallos de los italianos, y al final el Kids&Us acabó el periodo con un 82-70 que no dejó el partido sentenciado, pero sí encarrilado. En los últimos diez minutos, los manresanos buscaron sellar el choque lo antes posible y lo consiguieron después de unos muy buenos minutos de JD Notae, que puso el 89-71 en el marcador con un BC Roma completamente hundido y sin apenas opciones de remontar. Al final, el Kids&Us Manresa, a diferencia del resto de partidos de la actual temporada, fue el equipo que se fue más allá de los 100 puntos y se llevó el triunfo por 108-88 en un duelo plácido que se traduce en la segunda victoria esta temporada en la Eurocopa. 108. Kids&Us Manresa (32+25+25+26): Benitez (24), Notae (12), Agbo (3), Vila (5), Ongenda (20) -cinco inicial-; Kolenda (-), Beaufort (1), Bassas (13), Fernández (10), Oriola (19) y Minchev (1). 88. BC Roma (21+25+24+18): Mannion (21), Watson (5), Strautins (10), Ayayi (12), Simonovic (4) -cinco inicial-; Davis (8), Emejuru (2), Flowers (2), Stevenson (13) y Olynyk (11). Árbitros: Uros Obrknezevic, Amit Balak y Christopher Lemaire. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase regular de la Eurocopa de baloncesto disputado en el Nou Congost.

articles.title: LeBron James shrugs off criticism as his luxury commute becomes an NBA talking point
articles.summary: LeBron James threw down a huge dunk in his Sixers home debut and dismissed his helicopter commute as “just transportation.”
articles.body:
Few athletes live under a brighter spotlight than LeBron James. Every move he makes becomes a talking point within minutes. His new chapter in Philadelphia has already given fans plenty to talk and argue about.

One evening produced two very different conversations. One was about pure basketball joy, and the other was about logistics, money, and image. Together they show how a single big night can carry both celebration and criticism.

LeBron James took the Philadelphia floor on Friday, October 16, and performed his famous chalk toss before tipoff. A sellout crowd of 19,746 packed Xfinity Mobile Arena for the 76ers' preseason finale against Boston.

In the first quarter, Tyrese Maxey lobbed a half-court pass to James, who finished the play with a two-handed alley-oop dunk that sent the crowd into a frenzy. It offered Sixers fans an early look at the transition connection Philadelphia hopes to use this season.

James finished with 8 points, 8 rebounds and 7 assists in 25 minutes. Boston won 125-120 in overtime at Xfinity Mobile Arena, ending Philadelphia's preseason with a loss.

Tyrese Maxey started the play with a long pass in LeBron's direction. James locked eyes on the ball right away. He snared it and finished at the rim with ease for all the home fans.

Maxey is a close friend of James. LeBron has credited him with swaying the decision to sign in Philadelphia. The two now want to run the floor and score in transition as often as possible.

After the game, James said the team is still finding its rhythm. He noted they are only a couple of weeks in together. He admitted some kinks remain, but said plenty exists to build on.

On July 24, James announced that he would join Philadelphia after his agent, Rich Paul, held conversations with 27 NBA teams during the free-agency process. James agreed to a reported two-year, $8 million deal. The Sixers have not won an NBA championship since 1983.

Fanatics Fest ran from July 16-19 in New York, and James appeared at the event on July 16. Five days after the festival ended, he announced his decision to join Philadelphia. James already had a separate long-term business relationship with Fanatics through a trading-card partnership signed in 2024.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro proclaimed July 24 as LeBron James Day following the announcement. The designation reflected the considerable attention James' move generated across Philadelphia and Pennsylvania.

James is splitting his time between the Philadelphia area and New York City. He has used a helicopter to travel between New York and the Sixers' facilities near their Camden, New Jersey, practice site.

Front Office Sports reported that a typical one-way helicopter trip takes about 30 minutes, compared with roughly 90 minutes to 2 hours by car. Other reporting has placed the helicopter journey at approximately 30-45 minutes, depending on the trip.

The arrangement significantly reduces James' travel time between the two areas. During a demanding NBA season, avoiding lengthy road trips can free up additional time for basketball preparation, recovery, and personal commitments.

LeBron is not paying for the flights. His spokesperson told Front Office Sports that the Fanatics deal includes access to its corporate aviation. Reports say that similar trips run about $4,000 to $10,000 each way.

The arrangement also serves Fanatics. A branded helicopter carrying a global star gets attention every time it lands. Sponsors like that kind of visibility, and fans notice it quickly on social media and in headlines.

The perk also explains why the ride has become such a big topic. A famous player, a big sponsor, and a busy commute make an easy story. Fans naturally want to know exactly who pays.

Little-known fact: During a July 2026 conversation at Fanatics Fest, James explained that his growing interest in golf also connects to his broader ambitions in business and philanthropy.

After the Celtics game on Friday night, James addressed the helicopter talk for the first time. He also said he has done it before. He simply called it "Just another way of transportation. That's all."

Those were his first public comments on the rides. He is dismissing the concerns and insists it is much ado about nothing. The story had been building for over a week.

His short answer keeps the story simple. Stars often avoid long explanations when a topic feels overblown. Still, the helicopter will probably stay in the headlines every time it lifts off near Camden or Manhattan.

At 41, James is heading into a record 24th season and his first with Philadelphia. He spent the previous eight years with the Lakers. One lob and a dunk made the arena feel brand new.

Philadelphia also added Jaylen Brown by trade. He joins Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey on a roster that now threatens the reigning champion New York Knicks in the East. That depth raises expectations across Philadelphia.

One preseason game offers thin evidence. Still, James looked active as a finisher and a passer, a balance that has defined his career. It should keep Philadelphia fans very optimistic about the season ahead.

The real test begins when games count. Preseason highlights fade fast, and opponents will adjust. The Sixers must turn flashes of chemistry into steady wins across a long season of constant travel and heavy scrutiny.

The helicopter story will follow him. Each ride will invite questions about cost, safety, and focus. Winning is usually the surest way to quiet outside noise. A strong start would make the commute seem minor.

For fans, the picture is simple. A veteran legend, a speedy guard, and a hungry city make a fun mix. Whether the helicopter lands softly or loudly, the season has real buzz and big hopes.

LeBron's two-handed dunk off a Maxey pass electrified a sellout crowd of 19,746.

He calls his helicopter rides "just another way of transportation."

Fanatics covers the flights as part of his existing deal.

The Sixers now face the real test of turning chemistry into wins.

articles.title: Pistons storm back from 22-point hole to spoil Paul George’s historic Celtics debut, win NBA’s season opener
articles.summary: The NBA season tips off in Detroit as the Celtics face the Pistons.
articles.body: Paul George made history in his Boston Celtics debut. But it wasn’t enough to fend of the determined Detroit Pistons.The Pistons looked down and out at home in Tuesday’s NBA season opener as the Celtics opened a 72-50 third-quarter lead. But they stormed back to secure a stunning, 121-113 win.Sparked by Duncan Robinson and Javonte Green off the bench, the Pistons caught fire from 3 and reeled off a 23-0 fourth-quarter run to turn a 99-89 deficit into a 112-99 lead.The dizzied Celtics were out of responses. A Derrick White floater stopped the bleeding with 3:18 remaining. But the damage had been done. Detroit held on down the stretch to fire the opening salvo in what projects to be a highly competitive race in the Eastern Conference.The win spoiled a historic effort from Paul George. George led the Celtics to their 22-point lead and etched his name into Boston’s record book in the third quarter of his Celtics debut. With his 31st point in the third quarter, George set the scoring record for a player making his Celtics debut, topping Kristaps Porziņģis’ 30 points in his first game with Boston in 2023. He hit three consecutive 3-pointers in the third to extend the Boston lead. He finished with 38 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists and 5 steals as the game’s leading scorer while shooting 12 of 21 from the field and 7 of 12 from 3. But it was Detroit’s 3-point shooting and stifling defense down the stretch that made the difference in the game.Robinson shot 5 of 9 from 3 in a 21-point effort. Green shot 5 of 8 from 3 off the bench and scored all 17 of his points in the second half after not playing in the first. A Green 3 off a Pistons defense stop capped Detroit’s 23-0 fourth-quarter run.Javonte Green misses the shot, Jayson Tatum misses the layup on the fastbreak, slow to return on defense, and Javonte hits the triple to put the Pistons up 13 pic.twitter.com/f69KksDpbd— MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) October 20, 2026 In the end, the Pistons shot 17 of 42 (40.5%) from long distance after a 4-of-22 (18.2%) start to secure the comeback win.Jalen Duren tallied 22 points, 9 rebounds, 1 block and 1 steal while shooting 8 of 13 from the floor in a strong first effort since his protracted offseason contract standoff. Cade Cunningham, coming off a First-team All-NBA season, matched Duren with a team-high 22 points to go with 8 assists and 4 rebounds.While George feasted, Jayson Tatum struggled against Detroit’s stingy defense. The Celtics star finished with 13 points and 11 assists. He shot just 6 of 23 from the field and missed all seven of his 3s. He scored just two points after halftime after posting 11 in the first half.This story will be updated.

articles.title: Mississippi Valley State basketball player released from ICE custody on bond weeks after being detained
articles.summary: Qingfang Pang, who came to the United States from China three years ago, said he was unaware he had not filed the correct paperwork to renew his visa.
articles.body:
A Mississippi Valley State basketball player who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement several weeks ago was released on bond Tuesday afternoon.

Qingfang Pang, 21, came to the United States from China three years ago and is a member of the Mississippi Valley State men's basketball team. He was arrested Sept. 29 while trying to board a flight from Jackson, Mississippi, to New York. Pang had been detained by ICE in Louisiana ever since.

Pang's attorney, Marcus Session, told ESPN on Tuesday that he was the victim of a "procedural mistake." Pang's student visa expired last month, and he was unaware that he had not filed the correct paperwork to renew it.

Then, while he was detained, Session said Peng was "coerced" into signing a voluntary departure document by ICE officials. Session said that Peng, who has a limited knowledge of the English language, didn't understand the document he was signing. It has since been rescinded, and Peng wants to remain in Mississippi.

"He legally entered the U.S. on November 17, 2023 on a temporary basis not to exceed September 5, 2024, but illegally overstayed," the U.S. Department of Homeland Security said in a statement, via ESPN . "All of his claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and he will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law."

Pang, a 6-foot-9 forward, played high school basketball in New York. He transferred into Mississippi Valley State this past offseason after getting his start at Monroe University. Mississippi Valley State officials were the ones that discovered Pang's F-1 student visa had expired, and told him he had to leave campus. Session said he was on his way to his guardian's home in New York when he was arrested at the airport.

"He's a strong kid, but even a strong kid would have his emotions and faith tested," Session said.

Peng is the second college basketball player in the United States to be detained by ICE in recent weeks. Aminata Seck, a member of the Kentucky State women's basketball team , was detained in August. Seck, who is from Senegal, was released on bond on Oct. 7.
